tool_bg_d: Remove the background from any photo in one click.
tool_img_d: Shrink JPG, PNG, WEBP and AVIF images, one by one or in batches.
tool_pdf_d: Make PDF files smaller while keeping the text sharp and selectable.
ci_meta_title: Compress images online for free (JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF)
ci_meta_desc: Reduce the size of your JPG, PNG, WEBP and AVIF images without visible quality loss. Batch compression, resizing and format conversion, right in your browser: your photos never leave your device.
ci_lead: Shrink JPG, PNG, WEBP and AVIF files in seconds, one at a time or in batches. Pick the quality, resize if you need to, compare before and after, then download.
ci_hint: JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF or GIF · several at once · or paste with Ctrl+V
ci_q_hint: 75 to 85 is the sweet spot: much lighter files with no visible difference.
ci_strip: Metadata such as EXIF and GPS location is removed from compressed images.
cis1_d: Drop, paste or pick one or more photos. Nothing is uploaded.
cis2_d: Choose the format and quality, and resize if needed. The result updates instantly.
cis3_d: Save each image, or all of them at once in a ZIP file.
cia1: Compression removes details your eye can barely see. At a quality of 75 to 85, the difference is usually invisible while the file is often 50 to 80% lighter. Use the Compare button to check before you download.
cia2: WEBP is the best choice for websites and is supported by all modern browsers. AVIF is even lighter but slower to create and not accepted by every app. JPG works everywhere, including email and printing. PNG is for logos, screenshots and images with transparency.
ciq3: Are my images uploaded to a server?
cia3: No. Compression runs in your browser, on your device. Your images are never sent or stored anywhere.
ciq4: Is there a size or file limit?
cia4: There is no limit other than your device's memory. Very large images (over 50 megapixels) can be slow on a phone.
cp_meta_desc: Reduce the size of your PDF files right in your browser. Images are recompressed while text stays sharp and selectable. No upload, no sign-up, no watermark.
cp_lead: Make your PDFs small enough to email or upload. The images inside are recompressed, while text and drawings stay sharp and selectable.
cp_hint: One or several PDF files · nothing is uploaded
cp_l_light_d: High quality images (200 dpi). Good for printing.
cp_l_medium_d: Good balance (150 dpi). Ideal for email and screens.
cp_l_strong_d: Smallest file with selectable text (100 dpi).
cp_l_raster_d: Each page becomes a picture. Text can no longer be selected or searched.
cp_engine_note: The first time, your browser downloads the PDF engine (about 11 MB). It is then kept in cache.
cp_privacy: Your PDF is processed on your device and never uploaded: safe for confidential documents.
cps1_d: Drop or pick one or more PDF files.
cps2_d: Recommended suits most needs. Strong makes the smallest file while keeping the text.
cps3_d: Check the new size and save your lighter PDF.
cpq1: How much smaller will my PDF be?
cpa1: It depends on what is inside. PDFs full of photos or scanned pages often shrink by 70 to 95%. PDFs that contain only text (exported from Word, for example) are already compact: expect anywhere from 0 to 50%, sometimes nothing at all. If the result is not smaller, you get your original file back.
cpa2: Yes with the Light, Recommended and Strong levels: only the images are recompressed. Only the Pages as images mode turns each page into a picture.
cpq3: Are my files uploaded to a server?
cpa3: No. Compression runs in your browser with the open-source Ghostscript engine. Your documents never leave your device.
cpq4: Can I compress a password-protected PDF?
cpa4: No. Open it with its password and save a copy without protection first, then compress that copy.
tj_png_lossless: PNG without loss: same pixels, optimized file.
tj_png_colors: PNG reduced to {n} colors: much lighter, but photos may show banding.
tj_lossy: 75 to 85 is the sweet spot: much lighter files with no visible difference.
tj_engine: Downloading the PDF engine (first time only)…
tj_encrypted: This PDF is password-protected. Remove the protection first.
tj_damaged: This PDF seems damaged and can't be read.
